chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Misma'a Abu Sayyar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the time for the Dhuhr prayer on the day of Friday during travel. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'At the decline of the sun, and that is its time on the day of Friday, when not traveling.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific time for Friday Dhuhr prayer during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the time for Dhuhr on Friday is strictly at solar noon (zawal), regardless of whether one is traveling or resident, thereby refuting the notion of an extended or distinct Friday-specific window. This hadith is significant in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the precise moment for the 'gathering' (jam') of Dhuhr and Asr, emphasizing that the Friday prayer time does not differ from the general Dhuhr time in its onset. It underscores the principle that travel does not alter the fundamental timing of the prayer, only the manner of its performance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Misma’a Abu Sayyar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the time for Al-Zohr (Salāt) on the day of Friday during the journey. So heasws said: ‘At the (start of the) decline of the sun, and that is its time during the day of Friday, in other than a journey’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim from Misma’ abu Sayyar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the time for Salah (prayer) of al-Dhuhr on Friday on a journey. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is at Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime) which is its time on Friday when one is not on a journey.’”
